High-Growth in Northern Ireland
Mapping out the most ambitious 
businesses in Northern Ireland

We use 8 criteria to identify high-growth 
and ambitious companies. Each of these 
is a sign of external validation that a 
business is either actively growing or 
creating ambitious growth plans. 
All companies featured in this report have 
met at least one of these growth triggers.
What do we mean by “high-growth and “ambitious”?

Accelerator attendance

There are 612 active, ambitious 
companies in Northern Ireland.
An additional 31 have exited the market, 
either through an IPO or an acquisition, 
and 136 are no longer trading.  
The region has a strong base of 
established businesses. The seed stage is 
the most populated, with few companies 
having developed into the venture and 
growth stages of evolution.

Only 32% of high-growth companies in 
Northern Ireland have raised equity 
investment, far lower than the national 
average of 52%.
Instead, it has a very healthy population of 
scaleups: 32% of high-growth companies 
have achieved at least 10% scaleup status. 
The most common method of growth is 
attending an accelerator, the most popular of 
which was the now inactive Entrepreneurial 
Spark, powered by Ulster Bank Hatchery.

Methods of growth

£145m of equity investment has been 
deployed across 178 announced deals 
since 2011. 
A total of 246 companies in Northern 
Ireland have raised equity investment, 
100 of which have never announced 
their fundraisings to the media. 
2019 was a record year for Northern 
Ireland’s high-growth businesses, with 
more pounds invested over more deals 
than any year prior.

AdTech is the most common buzzword 
in Northern Ireland. This includes 
Péarlaí , which develops a software 
that allows shopping centres and 
retailers to track individual customers 
through physical stores, predict their 
buying behaviours, and send 
personalised oﬀers to their phones.
AI and Digital Security are also fairly 
strong areas, with 14 companies 
operating within each. 
NUMBER OF AMBITIOUS COMPANIES IN NORTHERN IRELAND
Sectors and verticals

Unsurprisingly, Belfast is the most saturated 
area of high-growth companies, with 234 
active ambitious companies operating in the 
city. Belfast is home to a far higher proportion 
of seed stage companies (45%) compared to 
the rest of the country (26%), as well as a 
higher proportion of dead companies (21% vs 
16%). This suggests that the capital is an 
incubator for the country’s riskiest ventures. 
Mid Ulster and Newry, Mourne and Down are 
the next most densely populated, whilst the 
West of the country is home to the fewest 
high-growth firms. 
DISTRIBUTION OF ACTIVE AMBITIOUS COMPANIES 
Geographical distribution

The country’s scaleups show a slightly 
more even geographical distribution. Mid 
Ulster ties with Belfast as the most densely 
populated district, each home to 43 visibly 
scaling businesses.  
More than half of scaleups in Mid Ulster  
operate within the industrial sector, 
primarily manufacturing building 
materials, furniture and machinery. In 
Belfast, the majority of scaleups are 
operating within the business and 
professional services sector, particularly in 
insurance, security and financial services. 
DISTRIBUTION OF 10% AND 20% SCALEUP COMPANIES 
Scaleups

31% of high-growth companies in 
Northern Ireland have a female founder, 
the second highest rate in the UK, after 
Scotland.  
82% of female founded businesses are 
in the seed stage of evolution, 
representing a strong pipeline of 
investable companies for the future. It 
remains to be seen if these businesses 
receive suﬀicient funding to progress 
through the next stages of evolution.
